title: Thinking CAPs Eclipse contribution compliance audit
verdict: Not all contributions are ready or demonstrably compliant. Two published native PRs have failing ECA gates; policy/checklist, commit metadata, disclosure, IP-review and evidence issues remain.
scope: The working 20-issue registry; selected current native patches and all referenced PR drafts; local and remote Git branch contribution records; GitHub native PRs #601/#40/#3307 and hackathon PRs #32/#33/#34; source notice scan outside imported evidence; the separately imported bug queue. No source code or original evidence was changed.
applicability: Official Eclipse project requirements apply to native contributions. Thinking_CAPs is an event repository: its status as an official Foundation-managed project repository was not established. Foundation requirements are used as upstream readiness criteria for its integration code, not asserted as automatic legal violations for every hackathon commit. Team README review/transparency promises apply to its work.
limits: This is an evidence and process audit, not legal clearance or complete semantic code/security review.
Native builds, hardware campaigns and model calls were not rerun. Recorded successes are subject-bound historical evidence.

Workspace imports changed concurrently during the audit. Audited Git refs are captured in audit-subject.json; measured manifest outputs describe the bytes when checked, not an atomic snapshot of the final mutable workspace.
Employer approval, confidential/PII prompt handling, provider terms, training use, indemnity conditions, plagiarism filtering and all third-party provenance cannot be certified from these artifacts.
No evidence establishes automatic AI merging. Missing review records do not prove that an offline review never occurred.
Encryption/cryptography applicability, official project committer status and IP review exemptions require the receiving project disposition.
Hackathon eligibility and organizer submission rules were not assessed.

findings.title: Two published upstream PRs fail Eclipse ECA validation
findings.observation: GitHub reports eclipsefdn/eca=failure for CDA PR #601 and inc_diagnostics PR #40. The official Eclipse validation pages specifically report that the author and committer Eclipse accounts cannot be found for their erupuri identity/email. Their branch submission checklists nevertheless mark ECA as DONE. This is an account/commit eligibility failure, not proof that the person never signed an agreement under another identity.
findings.corrective_action: The contributor must resolve account/agreement/email eligibility and obtain a passing PR ECA status. Correct the checklists to reflect the actual gate until it passes.

findings.title: Submission checklists incorrectly require no AI attribution
findings.observation: The CDA and diagnostics branch submission documents contain No AI Attribution= DONE / Clean commit message; the CDA checklist also calls No AI attribution=PASS. Neither retrieved upstream contribution guide requires hiding AI use. The published PRs and their commit messages contain no AI assistance disclosure. Significant AI use on these particular patches remains an authorship question, so missing disclosure is conditional; the written checklist rule is already wrong.
findings.corrective_action: Replace the invented no-attribution criterion with accurate AI disclosure. Establish whether meaningful AI was used and disclose it in the published contribution when applicable.

findings.title: AI tools are recorded as human coauthors
findings.observation: All five prepared Rust API mail patches (#1261, #250, #560, #781, #490) include Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. The hackathon Rust queue, ThreadX, X-COM and OpenBSW branch commits also use this trailer. Eclipse coauthor entries identify real contributors subject to agreement validation. These commits already disclose AI use; an Assisted-by trailer is the appropriate identity convention, not a legal AI coauthor.
findings.corrective_action: Use Assisted-by for AI tool identification in future/native submission commits. Preserve real human authors and historical evidence; do not silently rewrite shared history.

findings.title: AI disclosure does not consistently travel with native contributions
findings.observation: Known AI-assisted SOME/IP, lifecycle, communication #1265/#1167 and four bug-queue PR drafts omit an explicit assistance disclosure. All selected registered patches lack AI Disclosure/CC0-1.0 markers. Rust API mail messages do disclose DeepSeek and corrections in prose, which is positive. The lifecycle new macro is explicitly attributed to Fabro/Flash in its record but has only an Apache-2.0 header. Source files largely generated by AI need the handbook file disclosure treatment; the degree of generation must be confirmed per file. PR #3307 discusses AI tooling but does not explicitly disclose AI assistance in authoring that contribution.
findings.corrective_action: Add explicit tool/model disclosure to the intended native commits and PRs. Review new files for largely AI-generated content and apply the handbook header/disclosure example with the actual project licence. Do not relabel copied third-party code or blanket-convert the repository to CC0.

findings.title: Large native patches have no recorded Eclipse IP Team review
findings.observation: Patch additions are SOME/IP #84: 3198; communication #1261: 2132; #250: 1544; #560: 1976; OpenBSW transportRouter: 2353. Published diagnostics PR #40 adds 1503 lines. No corresponding IP review reference was found in the inspected records. The old five diagnostics patches add 2012 lines in total, including lock changes; they are not the same payload as PR #40. Added-line totals flag review candidates, not a legal calculation of net new IP. Generated/repeated content and committer status require project disposition.
findings.corrective_action: Ask the relevant project committer to evaluate net new content and the applicable IP review requirement; record the review/request and approval before official merging. Do not treat tests or splitting one contribution into smaller commits as IP approval.

findings.title: Diagnostics PR #40 lacks required DCO sign-offs
findings.observation: All three commits in inc_diagnostics PR #40 have no Signed-off-by trailer. Its current CONTRIBUTION.md explicitly requires both ECA and DCO. The SOME/IP and lifecycle artifacts are plain uncommitted diffs: absent trailers there are preparation items, not defective existing commits. S-CORE PR #3307 has a Signed-off-by trailer. Communication CONTRIBUTING.md does not itself explicitly mandate DCO, so no blanket DCO failure is asserted for that module.
findings.corrective_action: The actual contributor must supply the required truthful DCO certification for the diagnostics commits. Include it in future SOME/IP/lifecycle commits when preparing their submissions.

findings.title: Author names and ECA coverage need checking per native commit
findings.observation: Many root/prepared commits and PR #3307 use author name jnsagai; CDA #601 and diagnostics #40 use erupuri. Eclipse requires the author actual legal name and matching account email. These values look like login handles; they are not verified legal identities. The declared Eclipse username jnascimento6p0 has a current signed-ECA lookup result (HTTP 200). PR #3307 independently has a passing ECA check. Neither result validates every other contributor, every email, or the proposed AI coauthors.
findings.corrective_action: Use the responsible contributor legal name and registered email in native commits. Validate each native PR through its actual Eclipse ECA check rather than extending one username lookup to every contribution.

findings.title: The contribution registry cannot verify all submission records
findings.observation: scripts/verify_contributions.py --json exits 1 on diagnostics #16: registry observation date 2026-10-06 versus snapshot 2026-10-04. Both diagnostics and CDA recovered-patch paths are relative to contributions/ but actual files are under OpenSOVD/patches/. CDA lacks an evidence_manifest and upstream_snapshot field. Both are marked submission_candidate=true despite testing-pending records and no singular patch as expected by the verifier. The independently inspected #1265 engineering-review manifest contains one missing native-verification/execution/attempts/first-native-run/tools/bazel entry. Registered patches with declared SHA-256 values match; the remaining tested manifest entries match their captured hashes.
findings.corrective_action: Correct registry/path/date/schema inconsistencies using genuine current evidence; add a supported multi-patch representation and the missing CDA metadata. Restore the missing #1265 artifact or explicitly document and rework its portability binding. Preserve historical bytes and avoid marking untested recovered patches ready.

findings.title: Published contributions and branch packets are missing from the registry
findings.observation: The working registry has 20 entries and no recorded PR for CDA #543 or diagnostics #16, although current GitHub PRs #601 and #40 exist and branch submission documents name them. OpenBSW transportRouter, fault-storage write-through, receiver instrumentation, ThreadX/X-COM integration and the separately imported four-item communication bug queue are outside the registered issue inventory. Old CDA/diagnostics patches do not identify the current submitted revisions.
findings.corrective_action: Record current publication/head/base/status and evidence links for the published PRs. Add separate entries for distinct prepared contributions and distinguish submitted code from old recovered patches and integration examples.

findings.title: The root licence is abbreviated and source headers are inconsistent
findings.observation: Root LICENSE is a 15-line Apache notice, not the full Apache-2.0 terms; GitHub reports NOASSERTION for its detected licence. There is no root CONTRIBUTING file, including the inspected organization defaults. A scan of 111 tracked source/script files outside contribution/evidence imports found 68 without SPDX markers and no copyright ownership marker in their first 2500 characters. This set includes imported helper scripts and is not a declaration of authorship. In remote ThreadX PR #32, 3/19 added source/script files lack SPDX; in X-COM PR #33 all 9 inspected new Python files lack SPDX. Existing native S-CORE new-source headers are generally present. JSON configurations cannot use ordinary comment headers and need separate treatment.
findings.corrective_action: Supply the full intended licence and document contribution/AI/review requirements. Establish actual ownership/provenance before adding appropriate file notices. Preserve upstream MIT/Apache and other imported notices; use supported sidecars or licence metadata for formats without comments.

findings.title: Independent human review is not consistently recorded
findings.observation: SOME/IP/lifecycle records contain scoped local owner approval, which is positive but not upstream committer acceptance. Communication implementations and assessments explicitly retain pending acceptance. ThreadX PR #32 was merged by its author jnsagai and has no GitHub review or issue-comment records; X-COM PR #33 and Rust queue PR #34 also have no review records at retrieval. A human merge identity does not establish that an agent merged automatically, and an empty GitHub review list does not disprove an offline review. Root README requires another team member for critical changes and explicit human review of AI-modified code.
findings.corrective_action: Retain a real reviewer identity, reviewed revision and decision, including the additional reviewer required for critical changes. Keep human approval before official merges; do not infer it from agent reviews or test passes.

findings.title: Selected Linux evidence does not establish every native gate
findings.observation: The Rust API packets retain unrun QNX, test-code Clippy, sanitizers and analyzers; #1261 adds a Clippy warning and has scope/allocation/ABI questions. #250 has unresolved alignment with system-wide discovery; #560 retains warnings. #781 remains an ABI/ownership draft; #490 has never successfully run its test group. The four bug-queue latest proposals build and run 502 tests with 6 skips, but retain failed copyright checks and specific lint/analyzer/production-integration gaps. PR #3307 correctly retains an inherited failing docs check. OpenBSW lacks the full CI/toolchain/doc matrix and prior issue agreement. Fault-lib lacks full CI/pre-commit and human reproduction acceptance. Platform relevance must be disposed by maintainers, rather than automatically demanding every possible check.
findings.corrective_action: Resolve or obtain the project authorized disposition of failing required gates and scope questions. Rerun affected checks after source changes/rebases. Keep the unbuilt and incomplete proposals as drafts or assessments.

findings.title: Prework declaration conflicts with retained implementation dates
findings.observation: prework/README.md describes prework as research/design/documentation only and the contribution plan says no code written. Recovered diagnostic implementation commits are dated 2026-09-22 and diagnostic campaign evidence includes 2026-09-25, before the October 6 event start. The root README already promises to identify preexisting development. This is an internal transparency inconsistency; competition eligibility has not been established and no organizer-policy violation is asserted.
findings.corrective_action: Clarify original implementation versus event changes and keep actual dates. Verify organizer rules separately before claiming competition eligibility.

registered_contributions.assessment: Scoped owner approval and substantial native evidence retained; 3198 additions flag IP review, native AI disclosure and future DCO/author identity remain open.
113 recorded native cases and scoped owner approval; Flash-authored macro lacks file AI disclosure; future DCO and upstream acceptance pending.
Current submitted PR #40 differs from old recovered patches; ECA fails, all three commits lack DCO, checklist wrongly says no AI attribution; 1503 added lines flag IP review.

From 4760fe47f2edc25c16f7f76f70c68397feb90586 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001

Subject: [PATCH] Rust::com: Add async stream of newly available services

Addresses #1261.

Add Runtime::find_all_services(), an asynchronous stream of
interface-independent ServiceDescriptor items (service type name, version,
binding, binding service id and instance id).

The LoLa backend starts one find-any watch per service type present in the
loaded configuration (including add-on configurations merged before the
stream is opened) and reports any concrete provider instance id. Services
that are already offered are yielded first; an identity is yielded again
when it is re-offered after a withdrawal. Pending items are coalesced: at
most one item per currently offered identity, discarded if the service is
withdrawn before being polled, which bounds the backlog by the offered set.
The stream ends when it is dropped, which stops every native watch.
Discovery callbacks only hold a weak reference to the stream state.

IRuntime gains GetConfiguredServiceWildcardIdentifiers(), declared last
with a default implementation. Runtime serializes add-on configuration
merges with the wildcard enumeration and invalidates its cache; returned
identifiers stay valid in address-stable storage.

Adds LoLa backend unit tests and the all_services_stream ITF integration
test (initial offer, later offer, withdrawal, re-offer with exact
identities and duplicate detection).

Implemented with DeepSeek V4 Flash (Fabro) and corrected by Claude.
Open design points (configured-service scope, operational-phase
allocation) are raised on #1261.

Subject: [PATCH] Rust::com: Support typed FindServiceSpecifier::Any discovery

Addresses #250.

Replace the panic for FindServiceSpecifier::Any with typed, same-interface
Any discovery in the LoLa runtime. Interfaces register their LoLa wildcard
configuration; find_service and the async discovery path resolve Any
through native find-any (FFI find_service_any / start_find_service_any)
and return ServiceNotFound for unmapped, concrete or malformed
registrations. The async search stop guard is created synchronously after
a successful start, so a never-polled or cancelled future stops the native
search.

Adds LoLa unit tests and the consumer_any_apis ITF integration test.

This is typed same-interface discovery, not system-wide discovery of all
interfaces (see #1261).

Implemented with DeepSeek V4 Flash (Fabro).
